package middleware

import (
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"testing"

	"github.com/labstack/echo/v4"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
)

func TestNilTargetsNext(t *testing.T) {
	e := echo.New()
	c := e.NewContext(httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/", nil), httptest.NewRecorder())
	assert.Nil(t, NewRandomBalancer(nil).Next(c))
	assert.Nil(t, NewRoundRobinBalancer([]*ProxyTarget{}).Next(c))
	rb := NewRandomBalancer(nil)
	assert.True(t, rb.AddTarget(&ProxyTarget{Name: "a"}))
	assert.NotNil(t, rb.Next(c))
	assert.True(t, rb.RemoveTarget("a"))
	assert.Nil(t, rb.Next(c))
	rrb := NewRoundRobinBalancer(nil)
	assert.True(t, rrb.AddTarget(&ProxyTarget{Name: "a"}))
	assert.NotNil(t, rrb.Next(c))
	assert.True(t, rrb.RemoveTarget("a"))
	assert.Nil(t, rrb.Next(c))

	// middleware returns 503 instead of panicking
	e2 := echo.New()
	e2.Use(Proxy(NewRoundRobinBalancer(nil)))
	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	e2.ServeHTTP(rec, httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/", nil))
	assert.Equal(t, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, rec.Code)
}
EOF

arguments.text:
Fixed in middleware/proxy.go.

- `randomBalancer.Next` now returns `nil` when the target list is empty (instead of calling `rand.Intn(0)` → "invalid argument to Intn").
- `roundRobinBalancer.Next` now returns `nil` when the target list is empty (instead of `% 0` → integer divide by zero). It also takes the read lock like the random balancer, so it no longer reads `targets` concurrently with AddTarget/RemoveTarget.
- The Proxy middleware now returns `echo.ErrServiceUnavailable` (503) when the balancer yields no target, instead of dereferencing a nil target, so your handler can respond with a "no target available" error.

Verified: `go build ./...`, `go vet`, `go test -race ./...` all pass; the full pre-existing suite is still green (unchanged from baseline), and a scratch test confirmed both balancers return nil for empty/emptied target lists and the middleware answers 503.

arguments.text:
Fixed in router.go.

`Router.Find` used to seed the context with the *requested* path (`ctx.path = path`) and only overwrite it with the matched route's pristine path when a route node was reached. So on a miss the context kept the request URL as its "path". I removed that initial assignment, so `ctx.path` now only gets set (to `currentNode.ppath`, the registered route path) when the router actually lands on a route node; on a miss it stays whatever `Context#Reset` left it as, i.e. `""`.

Verified: requesting `/does-not-exist` with only `GET /users/:id` registered now gives `c.Path() == ""` in the error handler (404 still returned), while matched requests still report `/users/:id`. Full test suite (incl. `-race`) is green.

Fixed in context.go.

`Context#Scheme()` is documented as returning the HTTP protocol scheme, `http` or `https`, but it returned whatever the first non-empty forwarding header contained. Now each header (`X-Forwarded-Proto`, `X-Forwarded-Protocol`, `X-Url-Scheme`) is only accepted if its value really is `http` or `https` (case-insensitive, normalized to lower case); otherwise the check falls through to the next header and finally to the `http` default. `X-Forwarded-Ssl: on` and TLS still yield `https`.

So with `X-Forwarded-Proto: ftp` and `X-Url-Scheme: https` you now get `https`; with only `ftp` you get `http`. Full test suite (incl. `-race`) is green.

package middleware

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"testing"

	"github.com/labstack/echo/v4"
)

func TestZZGzipEmpty(t *testing.T) {
	e := echo.New()
	e.Use(Gzip())
	e.GET("/empty", func(c echo.Context) error { return c.String(http.StatusOK, "") })
	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/empty", nil)
	req.Header.Set(echo.HeaderAcceptEncoding, "gzip")
	e.ServeHTTP(rec, req)
	fmt.Printf("code=%d CE=%q CT=%q body=%q len=%d\n", rec.Code, rec.Header().Get("Content-Encoding"), rec.Header().Get("Content-Type"), rec.Body.String(), rec.Body.Len())
}
EOF
